column1: # tests/oracle/tz.tsv — the TZ values tools/tzoracle runs the time sets
# under (every set of sets.tsv that prints a time: -D, --timefmt), over
# main/ and times/ (tests/fixtures/mkfixtures), one value per line:
# TZ `(unset)` unsets it, `(empty)` sets it empty. `needs` is a file the
# row needs on the host (`-` for none): a row whose file is missing is a
# loud, counted SKIP (macOS has no right/ or posix/ zones). `env` is one
# TZDIR=VALUE for both sides (`-` for none; TZDIR is the only one).
# class v1: aspen agrees with tree byte for byte, and with the reference
# build under --ref (the bytes before and after a change).
# class tree: aspen agrees with tree; under --ref the row is not compared,
# because aspen changed there on purpose (the comment above it says why).
# class refuse: a leap-second zone (aspen#13). aspen refuses it by name:
# status 2, nothing on stdout, one diagnostic naming the zone; tree's
# answer is printed for the record; a listing with no time column
# TZDIR names the database: glibc and std.time read it, src/clock never did
